 Game News > Games > Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA VI dips as low as 23fps on base PS5 in heavy action, Digital Foundry finds
 Semir Omerovic Published: 11:45, 18 November 2026 Share this story: Digital Foundry GTA VI frame-rate dipping to low 20s on base PS5 during heavy explosions, according to Digital Foundry’s analysis Key Points from the Article
 Base PS5 struggles to maintain 30fps during normal play with minor dips, and can drop to 23fps sustained during heavy action scenes like explosions
 PS5 Pro maintains near-flawless 30fps with perfect frame pacing, only briefly dropping to 24fps in worst-case scenarios before recovering
 Both consoles render at 1440p internal resolution, but PS5 Pro's PSSR upscaling produces a convincing 4K image while base PS5 clearly looks like upscaled 1440p
 GTA VI frame-rate dipping to low 20s on base PS5 during heavy explosions, according to Digital Foundry’s analysis Digital Foundry’s technical analysis of GTA VI shows the base PS5 struggles to hold its 30fps target more often than the PS5 Pro, with frame rates dropping as low as 23fps during heavy explosions.
 Grand Theft Auto 6 's 30fps target was always going to be controversial, and now we know how well consoles actually hold it. According to Digital Foundry’s technical analysis, the base PS5 has a harder time than you might expect.

 Semir Omerovic NOVEMBER 18 
 Base PS5 dips below 30fps
 Digital Foundry found that the base PS5 struggles to hold 30fps more often than PS5 Pro, with small dips throughout normal play. They described these as “really very minor”, but said they noticeably detract from the experience.
 Things get worse in heavy action. When Digital Foundry went on a rampage with a grenade launcher, blowing up vehicles in the street, the base PS5’s frame rate dropped to as low as 23fps in their footage. Crucially, those drops were sustained, with the scene running below 30fps until the player left the area or died.
 Digital Foundry were careful to stress that this is a worst case scenario, not representative of the game’s average performance which was closer to 30fps. But as they put it, if you’re the kind of GTA player who just wants to run around blowing things up, “you might get performance like this”.
 PS5 Pro is “the best way to play”
 PS5 Pro owners have far less to worry about. Digital Foundry called it “the best way to play this game by far”, with a near-flawless 30fps, perfect frame pacing and smooth cutscenes. Over more than 50 hours on Pro, they didn’t see a single dip in normal play. Even in the same explosion-heavy scenario, the Pro only briefly dropped to 24fps before recovering, rather than staying below 30fps like the base console.
 Digital Foundry On PS5 Pro, the performance is nearly flawless 
 1440p on both consoles, but PSSR makes a big difference
 Interestingly, Digital Foundry found that both PS5 and PS5 Pro appear to render GTA VI at an internal resolution of 1440p. The difference is in upscaling: on Pro, PSSR produces an image that “convincingly passes for native 4K”, while the base PS5 clearly looks like a 1440p image with spatial upscaling.
 Both consoles use ray-traced global illumination and reflections, while PS5 Pro adds ray-traced shadows on top, which Digital Foundry say remove the chunky shadow artefacts seen on the base PS5.
 Overall, Digital Foundry called the performance “both acceptable yet a little disappointing”, but said they were more willing to forgive the 30fps cap given how far GTA VI pushes its visuals. They described it as “the single most visually striking game of the generation”.
 Grand Theft Auto VI is out now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S .
